comments: Seventh run in the leaky0125+2w+1 hardware-scheme series, and the second attempt at eliminating 2x16 activations entirely. The first attempt (encoder_depth=0) removed both down1/down2 strides so everything ran at 4x32 -- it collapsed, best val dice 0.2894, pinned at the trivial all-background floor (0.24972243043788214) from roughly epoch 108 through 294. This one satisfies the same no-2x16 constraint from the other direction: stem_stride=1 (new constructor param) keeps the input at native 8x64 through stem/stageA/dec_a/head_out, and encoder_depth=1 gives exactly one downsample hop to a 4x32 bottleneck. Resolution ladder is {8x64, 4x32} -- verified by forward hooks that no conv in the network emits a 2x16 activation. Independent motivation beyond the constraint: with stem_stride=2 the head predicts at 4x32 and the logits are nearest-upsampled to 8x64, so every 2x2 block of the output is identical and the model cannot localize a target within a 2x2 cell -- a hard dice cap at this resolution, where a UAV target is only a couple of cells wide. stem_stride=1 removes that final upsample entirely (head_out predicts per-pixel at 8x64), which also means one fewer on-chip upsample stage for the NPU. Cost: every stage runs at 4x the spatial footprint, so ~3.3M vs 0.83M MACs (still 0.5% of the 640M budget) and peak activation buffer rises to ~32KB at the concat (still under cfg_gen.py's 0x12200=74240B per-buffer size, but 4x the previous footprint -- relevant if SRAM area, not MAC budget, is the binding constraint). Same finetune init (kurals/expand_kernel3.py; shape-compatible since stride isn't a learned parameter -- verified strict=True) and same stable quant_freeze_iters=76000 as the prior runs.
